summary: I am working on whether the rules that layer-pruning methods use to pick which layers to skip also pick the layers that make a language model refuse harmful requests, and how much speed I can gain before the refusals drop.
I am working on whether a replicated approximate-nearest-neighbour index silently diverges in search quality across replicas under node failure, and whether that divergence persists after recovery.
I am working on whether a pre-registered equivalence test can certify that a search scaffold adds nothing over budget-matched restarts of its own base searcher, and how often such a verdict is wrong.
